answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I can't tell you whether it's your IT band, and a guess wouldn't help you. Pain on the outside of the knee that is sharper on downhills is a pattern a physio or sports medicine doctor can sort out by examining you, so book that this week. Until then, treat it as an unassessed knee: no hills, no speed, no long run.

No, skip Wednesday's tempo, and don't swap in a shorter or easier version. The pain rose across the week and now shows up on stairs, so hard running waits until you have been seen and walking and stairs are pain-free.

new.analysis:
## What happened

Tuesday to Saturday went to plan, including Wednesday's threshold session: 4 mi at about 8:00/mi inside an 8 mi run. The knee gave its first signal as a 2/10 tightness on Thursday's last hill, and it was tight before Saturday's run started. On Sunday it turned sharp on the downhills from mile 7, and the 13 mi long run ended at 8.5 mi with a walk home.

## Why the plan changes this much

Pain that rises over four days and then shows up on stairs the next morning is more than normal training soreness. The knee reacted to hills and downhills both times, so those come out of the plan. I would rather give up a week of mileage now than push on and lose a month later.

The return to running is built as a test. Each short run is allowed only if the knee was fine the day before, and each one tells us whether the next is safe. If a test run goes badly, the next day becomes a walk, not a second attempt.

## What the missed miles cost

You are 10 weeks out and you already have a 12 mi long run from Aug 9. A lighter week was due after three building weeks anyway, so losing a week of load costs little against a 3:45 target, which needs about 8:35/mi on race day. Don't make up the missed 13 miles. Once you are assessed and cleared, I would rebuild the long run from 8 to 10 mi and move the marathon-pace segments back a couple of weeks.

## Your zones

Your easy share of 76% was fine for a week with a tempo, because the warm-up, cool-down and recovery jogs count as harder time. Nothing needs to change there. The heart rate cap of 145 on the short runs just keeps them clearly easy while the knee is being tested.

safetyCallouts.body: The pain rose from 2/10 to 4/10 over four days, was sharp on downhills, and now aches on stairs. See a physio or sports medicine doctor, and stop running if the pain returns or gets worse.

safetyCallouts.title: Get seen quickly if the knee changes.
safetyCallouts.body: If it swells, locks, gives way, wakes you at night, or hurts walking on flat ground, seek medical care promptly instead of waiting for the appointment.
